prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we work out 2 + 3 first?

steps.title: Look inside the brackets
steps.explanation: The brackets group 2 + 3 together.
steps.detail: Work out this group before multiplying.

steps.title: Brackets come first
steps.explanation: First, focus on 2 + 3.
steps.detail: Keep the 6 and the multiplication sign where they are.

steps.title: Work out the group
steps.explanation: 2 + 3 = 5. Replace the bracketed group with 5.
steps.detail: The value of the group stays the same.

steps.title: Now multiply
steps.explanation: We now have 6 × 5.
steps.detail: That means six groups of five.

notation.spoken: 6 times open bracket 2 plus 3 close bracket

lessons.objective: Interpret signed arithmetic as controlled movement on a number line.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Confusing the operation sign with the sign of the number.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Which direction did we move, and why?

steps.title: Start at the first number
steps.explanation: Start at 2 on the number line.

steps.title: Move left: 1 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to 1.

steps.title: Move left: 2 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to 0.

steps.title: Move left: 3 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to -1.
steps.detail: We have passed zero. Negative numbers are below zero.

steps.title: Move left: 4 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to -2.
steps.detail: We have passed zero. Negative numbers are below zero.

steps.title: Move left: 5 of 5
steps.explanation: Subtracting moves left. One step takes us to -3.
steps.detail: We have passed zero. Negative numbers are below zero.

steps.title: The answer is -3
steps.explanation: Five steps left from 2 reach −3.

lessons.objective: Interpret signed arithmetic as controlled movement on a number line.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Confusing the operation sign with the sign of the number.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Which direction did we move, and why?

steps.title: Start at the first number

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Start at 4 on the number line.

steps.title: Move left: 1 of 3

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Adding a negative moves left. One step takes us to 3.

steps.title: Move left: 2 of 3

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Adding a negative moves left. One step takes us to 2.

steps.title: Move left: 3 of 3

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

steps.explanation: Adding a negative moves left. One step takes us to 1.

steps.title: The answer is 1

left.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket equals 1

steps.explanation: The + tells us to add; −3 is the number being added. Three steps left from 4 reach 1.

notation.spoken: 4 plus open bracket minus 3 close bracket

lessons.objective: Multiply before adding when there are no brackets.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Which operation must we do before adding?

steps.title: Look at the two operations
steps.explanation: There is addition and multiplication. Multiplication comes first.

steps.title: Focus on multiplication
steps.explanation: Work out 3 × 2 before adding 4.

steps.title: Replace the product with six
steps.explanation: 3 × 2 is 6. Now we have 4 + 6.

lessons.objective: See that equal fractions shade the same amount of the same whole.
prerequisites: Read the symbols in this example

tutorNotes.observe: Ask the student to describe what changed before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Thinking a larger denominator means a larger shaded amount.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Did the shaded amount change when we added the dividing lines?

steps.title: Shade half of one whole
steps.explanation: The whole is split into two equal parts. One part is shaded.

steps.title: Split each half in two
steps.explanation: Divide each half into two equal parts. The shaded area stays the same.

steps.title: Compare the same sized wholes
steps.explanation: One of two parts is the same amount as two of four parts.

lessons.title: Three quarters of 20
lessons.label: Three quarters of 20
lessons.objective: Divide a quantity by the denominator, then select the numerator of equal groups.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Dividing by the numerator instead of making denominator-many equal groups.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we make four equal groups before selecting three?

steps.title: Start with twenty
steps.explanation: We want three of four equal parts of twenty counters.

scene.description: Twenty unit counters.

steps.title: Split into four equal parts

left.text: twenty divided by four equals five
left.spoken: twenty divided by four equals five

steps.explanation: Four equal groups give five counters in each quarter.

scene.description: Four equal quarters, each with five counters.

steps.title: Select three of the four quarters
steps.explanation: Select three groups of five. Three quarters of twenty is fifteen.

scene.description: Three of four quarters are highlighted; fifteen counters are selected.

lessons.title: 25% of 80
lessons.label: 25% of 80
lessons.objective: Connect twenty-five percent with one quarter of the original whole.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Treating twenty-five percent as twenty-five objects for every original amount.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the whole amount matter when finding twenty-five percent?

steps.title: Twenty-five percent is one quarter

left.text: twenty-five percent equals twenty-five hundredths equals one quarter
left.spoken: twenty-five percent equals twenty-five hundredths equals one quarter

steps.explanation: Percent means parts per hundred. Twenty-five of a hundred is one quarter.

scene.description: Four equal cards of value twenty represent the whole eighty.
scene.caption: Each card represents 20, not one unit.

steps.title: Split the whole into four equal parts

left.text: eighty divided by four equals twenty
left.spoken: eighty divided by four equals twenty

steps.explanation: Divide the whole eighty into four equal groups. Each quarter is twenty.

scene.description: Four equal parts each have value twenty.
scene.caption: Each card represents 20.

steps.title: Take one quarter

left.text: twenty-five percent of eighty equals twenty
left.spoken: twenty-five percent of eighty equals twenty

steps.explanation: Select one of the four equal parts. Twenty-five percent of eighty is twenty.

scene.description: One quarter of the whole eighty is selected: twenty.
scene.caption: Each card represents 20.

lessons.title: Add equal-denominator fractions
lessons.label: Add equal-denominator fractions
lessons.objective: Count equal fractional units while keeping the whole fixed.
prerequisites: Count small quantities and read the mathematical symbols used here.

tutorNotes.observe: Pause after each change. Ask the student to explain the picture before continuing.
tutorNotes.misconception: Adding denominators and changing the size of the fractional unit.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the denominator stay six when we add sixths?

steps.title: Six equal parts make one whole
steps.explanation: Each card stands for one sixth of the same whole. There are six equal parts.

scene.description: Six equal cards represent the six sixths of one whole.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

steps.title: Select the first sixth
steps.explanation: Select one of the six equal parts.

scene.description: One of six equal parts is highlighted.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

steps.title: Add two more sixths

left.text: one sixth plus two sixths equals three sixths
left.spoken: one sixth plus two sixths equals three sixths

steps.explanation: Add two more parts of the same size. Three sixths are now selected; the whole still has six parts.

scene.description: Three of six equal parts are highlighted.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

steps.title: Three sixths is half
steps.explanation: Three of six equal parts cover half the whole. The denominator was not added.

scene.description: Exactly half of the six parts are highlighted.
scene.caption: Each card is one sixth of this whole.

lessons.title: Square numbers
lessons.label: Square numbers
lessons.objective: Explain squaring as a square array and repeated multiplication.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Confusing three squared with three times two.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the small two give two factors of three?

steps.title: Read the exponent
steps.explanation: The small two means two factors of three. It does not mean three times two.

scene.description: An empty three-by-three grid.

steps.title: Build row 1
steps.explanation: Make the first row of three tiles. There are now 3 tiles.

scene.description: 1 filled rows of three tiles, 3 tiles in total.

steps.title: Build row 2
steps.explanation: Make a second row of three tiles. There are now 6 tiles.

scene.description: 2 filled rows of three tiles, 6 tiles in total.

steps.title: Build row 3
steps.explanation: Make a third row of three tiles. There are now 9 tiles.

scene.description: 3 filled rows of three tiles, 9 tiles in total.

steps.title: A square of nine tiles

left.text: three squared equals three times three equals nine
left.spoken: three squared equals three times three equals nine

steps.explanation: Three rows of three make nine square tiles. Squaring repeats a factor, not addition.

scene.description: A complete three-by-three square of nine tiles.

lessons.title: Cube numbers
lessons.label: Cube numbers
lessons.objective: Interpret a cube as two layers of a two-by-two array.
prerequisites: Understand square arrays and repeated multiplication.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Interpreting cubed as multiplying by three.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: What does the third factor of two count?

steps.title: Three factors of two
steps.explanation: The small three means multiply three factors of two.

scene.description: The first empty two-by-two layer.
scene.caption: Each tile represents one unit cube.

steps.title: Build the first layer
steps.explanation: One layer has two rows of two: four unit cubes.

scene.description: One two-by-two layer contains four unit cubes.
scene.caption: Each tile represents one unit cube.

steps.title: Add a second equal layer

left.text: two times two times two equals eight
left.spoken: two times two times two equals eight

steps.explanation: The third factor counts layers. Two layers of four make eight unit cubes.

scene.description: Two equal layers of four unit cubes make eight.
scene.caption: Two layers form a cube two units along each edge.

steps.title: Two cubed is eight
steps.explanation: The cube is two units wide, two high and two deep. There are eight unit cubes altogether.

scene.description: Eight unit cubes in two layers.
scene.caption: This flat drawing separates the two layers for clarity.

lessons.title: Square roots
lessons.label: Square roots
lessons.objective: Reverse a square array to find its positive side length.
prerequisites: Understand side length and square area.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Dividing twenty-five by two, or writing plus-or-minus five as the value of the square-root symbol.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why is a square root a side length rather than half an area?

steps.title: Start with twenty-five tiles
steps.explanation: The square root asks for the nonnegative side length of a square with this area.

scene.description: A square containing twenty-five equal tiles.

steps.title: Count one row
steps.explanation: One row contains five equal tiles.

scene.description: The first row of five tiles is highlighted.

steps.title: Check the equal sides
steps.explanation: The square is five tiles across and five high. Its area is twenty-five.

scene.description: Five rows of five tiles confirm the area twenty-five.

steps.title: Undo squaring

left.text: square root of twenty-five equals five
left.spoken: square root of twenty-five equals five

steps.explanation: The square-root symbol gives five, the nonnegative root. Solving an equation such as x squared equals twenty-five is a separate question.

scene.description: The square root gives the side length five.

lessons.title: Zero powers
lessons.label: Zero powers
lessons.objective: Extend a nonzero-base power pattern consistently by division.
prerequisites: Repeated multiplication; division by a nonzero number.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Thinking power zero makes the answer zero.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why must the next value be one to keep this pattern consistent?

steps.title: Begin with three factors

left.text: five cubed equals one hundred and twenty-five
left.spoken: five cubed equals one hundred and twenty-five

steps.explanation: Five times five times five is one hundred and twenty-five.

scene.description: The first 1 values of the pattern five cubed, five squared, five, and five to power zero.
scene.caption: Lower the exponent by one: divide the value by five.

steps.title: Remove one factor by division

left.text: one hundred and twenty-five divided by five equals twenty-five, five squared
left.spoken: one hundred and twenty-five divided by five equals twenty-five, five squared

steps.explanation: Lower the exponent from three to two. Divide the value by five.

scene.description: The first 2 values of the pattern five cubed, five squared, five, and five to power zero.
scene.caption: Lower the exponent by one: divide the value by five.

steps.title: Lower the exponent again

left.text: twenty-five divided by five equals five, five to power one
left.spoken: twenty-five divided by five equals five, five to power one

steps.explanation: Lowering from two to one divides by five again.

scene.description: The first 3 values of the pattern five cubed, five squared, five, and five to power zero.
scene.caption: Lower the exponent by one: divide the value by five.

steps.title: Keep the same division pattern

left.text: five divided by five equals one, five to power zero
left.spoken: five divided by five equals one, five to power zero

steps.explanation: One more division by five gives one. Every nonzero number to power zero is one. This pattern does not use a base of zero.

scene.description: The first 4 values of the pattern five cubed, five squared, five, and five to power zero.
scene.caption: Lower the exponent by one: divide the value by five.

lessons.title: Multiply powers
lessons.label: Multiply powers
lessons.objective: Count equal-base factors to explain addition of exponents.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Multiplying the exponents, or using this rule when adding powers.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we add the exponents rather than multiply them?

steps.title: Read the two powers
steps.explanation: The first power has three factors of two. The second has two factors of two.

scene.description: Three factors: 3 factors of two. Two factors: 2 factors of two
scene.caption: Each card is a factor of two, not an amount to add.

steps.title: Put all five factors together

left.text: two times two times two, times two times two
left.spoken: two times two times two, times two times two

steps.explanation: Multiplying the powers joins their factor lists. None of the factors change.

scene.description: Five factors: 5 factors of two
scene.caption: Each card is a factor of two, not an amount to add.

steps.title: Count factors in the exponent

left.text: two to power three plus two equals two to power five
left.spoken: two to power three plus two equals two to power five

steps.explanation: There are five factors of the same base. Add the exponents because you are counting factors.

scene.description: Five factors: 5 factors of two
scene.caption: Each card is a factor of two, not an amount to add.

steps.title: Check by multiplying

left.text: two to power five equals thirty-two
left.spoken: two to power five equals thirty-two

steps.explanation: Five factors of two multiply to thirty-two. This rule needs the same base and multiplication between the powers.

scene.description: Five factors: 5 factors of two
scene.caption: Each card is a factor of two, not an amount to add.

lessons.title: Prime factorisation
lessons.label: Prime factorisation
lessons.objective: Split composite factors until every leaf factor is prime.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Including composite parent nodes as extra factors, or calling one a prime.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why do we read only the leaves of the finished tree?

steps.title: Start with the whole number
steps.explanation: Find a product of prime numbers equal to eighteen.

scene.description: Visible factor nodes: 18. Selected prime factors: .

steps.title: Split eighteen into factors
steps.explanation: Two times nine is eighteen. Two is prime; nine can be split further.

scene.description: Visible factor nodes: 18, 2, 9. Selected prime factors: 2.

steps.title: Split the composite factor
steps.explanation: Nine is three times three. Both threes are prime.

scene.description: Visible factor nodes: 18, 2, 9, 3, 3. Selected prime factors: 2, 3, 3.

steps.title: Read only the prime leaves

left.text: eighteen equals two times three times three, or two times three squared
left.spoken: eighteen equals two times three times three, or two times three squared

steps.explanation: The prime factors multiply to eighteen. Do not multiply the parent nine again; its two children already replace it.

scene.description: Visible factor nodes: 18, 2, 9, 3, 3. Selected prime factors: 2, 3, 3.

lessons.title: Multiply by ten
lessons.label: Multiply by ten
lessons.objective: Multiply each digit value by ten by changing its place, not moving the decimal point.

tutorNotes.observe: Let the student describe the visible change before selecting Next.
tutorNotes.misconception: Teaching that the decimal point moves rather than digits changing place.
tutorNotes.checkQuestion: Why does the three now represent thirty rather than three?

steps.title: Read each digit value

left.text: three point four equals three plus four tenths
left.spoken: three point four equals three plus four tenths

steps.explanation: Three is in the ones column. Four is in the tenths column.

scene.description: Digit three is in ones and four is in tenths; the decimal boundary is fixed.
scene.caption: The decimal point stays fixed. The digits change place.

steps.title: Multiply every digit value by ten

left.text: three point four times ten equals thirty-four
left.spoken: three point four times ten equals thirty-four

steps.explanation: Each digit moves one column left: ones become tens, and tenths become ones. The decimal point stays fixed.

scene.description: The same digit three is now in tens and four is in ones; the decimal boundary stays fixed.
scene.caption: The decimal point stays fixed. The digits change place.

steps.title: Read the new value
steps.explanation: Three tens and four ones make thirty-four. The digits stay the same; their place values change.

scene.description: The same digit three is now in tens and four is in ones; the decimal boundary stays fixed.
scene.caption: The decimal point stays fixed. The digits change place.
